item.description:

Heavy storms have flooded tens of thousands of tents in Gaza, leaving many displaced in lethal conditions as aid distribution stalls. UNRWA funding cuts have deepened hardship for Palestinian refugees in Lebanon, while restrictions on aid have left Gaza families struggling to keep warm, with a baby reported to have died from cold. The United Nations reported 21,440 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.description:
The Sudanese army has seized the towns of Bakori and Sali in West Kordofan while the Rapid Support Forces continue drone strikes that have killed civilians in the Blue Nile and White Nile, including a strike that killed nine civilians in the Blue Nile. Drones now account for two thirds of child casualties in the conflict and a senior RSF commander defected to the army after 13 years of service. Vinícius Jr of Real Madrid sent a surprise video message to a Sudanese boy who received prosthetic legs after a drone strike. There were 4,680 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

UN peacekeepers were accused of failing to protect civilians before the Abiemnom massacre that killed at least 213 people, prompting Amnesty International to call for investigations. item.title: Ethiopia: the situation
item.description:
Federal forces have seized additional Tigray cities while fighting continues, and severe drought and prolonged conflict are driving acute hunger in Amhara, Tigray and Afar. Ethiopian drones are now operating over Sudan and RSF drones are launching from Ethiopian territory against Sudanese targets, prompting diplomatic expulsions and consular closures. An RPG strike near a school in Moyale killed dozens of Ethiopian Orthodox believers and a Kenyan, and attacks on Orthodox Christians persist in Arsi, Benishangul Gumuz and the north, with blasts heard in Addis Ababa. Seed insecurity threatens Tigray farmers and a psychosocial and spiritual care pilot is being tested, while displacement exceeds 50,000 people, and 2,824 battle-related deaths occurred in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.description:

Protesters also assaulted opposition supporters with chairs in Lagos, leading police to open a probe into the incident. Separately, police in Imo began investigating a suspected cult killing.
